General Staff: More troops return from AWOL in August than leave their units
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:42:00 UTC
06:42:00 KST

General Staff: More troops return from AWOL in August than leave their units
This was reported to Ukrinform by Lieutenant Volodymyr Molodii, spokesperson for the Human Capital Directorate of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
“In August 2026, the number of service members who returned to duty after AWOL exceeded the number of those who left their military units without authorization,” Molodii said.
He added that these figures demonstrate the new approaches introduced by the newly appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapatyi.
The spokesperson said that, in order to recruit conscripts and other eligible citizens for military service more effectively, four recruitment centers began operating in August under the West, East, South, and North operational commands. They are subordinate to the Ground Forces and operate within the areas of direct responsibility of the respective commands.
“The centers do more than simply offer positions in military units. They provide comprehensive information and support throughout the entire process of joining the Armed Forces – from selecting a position and preparing documents to undergoing the military medical examination and arriving at the place of service. The goal is to make every step a person takes toward military service fully clear and predictable,” Molodii explained.
He noted that the recruitment centers are one of the tools helping attract eligible citizens to serve under contract in the Armed Forces of Ukraine. He also recalled that in June, the Ministry of Defense, in cooperation with the General Staff, launched new incentive-based contracts with fixed terms of service: six to 14 months for infantry positions and 24 months for non-combat positions.
“The new contracts guarantee the right to discharge after the contract term has been completed, regardless of whether martial law remains in effect. This is an important step toward a model in which a person understands the basic conditions and prospects of military service even before joining,” Molodii emphasized.
At the same time, he noted that the issue of completing military service must be addressed together with rotation, force generation, training, and the recruitment of new personnel. The simultaneous discharge of a large number of service members without sufficient resources to replace them could directly affect the military’s combat capability. Therefore, the goal of personnel policy is not simply to set a discharge date, but to build a mechanism that will allow personnel to be gradually renewed, rotations to be ensured, and the required strength and capabilities of combat units to be maintained.
“The Commander-in-Chief has set the direction, while the specific tasks, indicators, and mechanisms for implementing it must be developed and formalized through separate decisions. At this stage, the relevant structural units of the General Staff continue their work in close cooperation with the Ministry of Defense,” Molodii said.
As reported by Ukrinform, the simplified procedure is available to service members of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, the National Guard, and the State Special Transport Service whose AWOL was recorded on or before June 12, 2026.

Embassy in Lima defends US$30 billion investment stock and takes aim at visa curbs as Fujimori joins Trump’s Shield of the Americas
4-MIN READ4-MIN
19
 Listen
Igor Patrickin Rio de Janeiro
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held talks in Peru on Thursday on countering Beijing’s growing footprint around the strategic Chancay megaport, drawing a sharp response from China’s embassy in Lima, which defended its investments and took aim at Washington’s strict visa rules.
Rubio met President Keiko Fujimori at the Government Palace, where she confirmed Peru would join the Shield of the Americas, a US-led coalition against organised crime. The Peruvian capital was the last stop of a three-day tour that also took him to Colombia and Ecuador.
Fujimori, a conservative who took office in July, has courted Washington on security while protecting its trade with China, which buys 35 to 38 per cent of Peruvian exports.
“Projects backed by the Chinese Communist Party bypass Peru’s legal frameworks and pose risks to transparency and data security,” Rubio wrote in the Peruvian newspaper El Comercio ahead of the visit.
In its statement on Tuesday, the embassy said China had “never interfered in the internal affairs of other countries” and “never demanded that other countries take sides”.
“The western hemisphere is nobody’s backyard,” it added.

Zelenskyy announces plans to sign Drone Deal with Canada
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher

Zelenskyy announces plans to sign Drone Deal with Canada
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that Ukraine expects to sign the so-called Drone Deal with Canada on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York at the end of September.
Source: European Pravda, citing the Zelenskyy's comments to journalists after his meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney
Details: Zelenskyy said that the countries had taken the first step towards signing the Drone Deal on Thursday 10 September, with Kyiv hoping to conclude the agreement this month.
"We signed the first step, and our teams told us that in 90 days we can have a drone deal. Then Mark said, 'Can we have it in nine days?' And the teams immediately said, 'Yes, of course.' Good proposition. And that's why I think we need to have meetings often," Zelenskyy said.
The president said that during his visit to Canada on 10 September, the two countries had signed a document launching joint drone production. The Canadian prime minister, for his part, announced that Canada will increase drone production and provide one-third of the output to Ukraine.
"We signed the beginning of our co-production of drones and 30% of these drones will go to Ukraine, immediately to the battlefield, immediately to our people. Our soldiers will have to save our children, our families, first of all. And this is very important," Zelenskyy said.
"I hope that in New York we can have such a big deal between our countries," he added.
Background:
- During a meeting with Zelenskyy, Carney said Canada would allocate C$350 million (US$253 million) to purchase interceptor missiles for Ukraine's air defence systems and announced plans to supply drones.
- On 10 September, Zelenskyy and Carney signed a declaration on a 100-year partnership, which expresses the two countries' intention to elevate bilateral relations to the level of a comprehensive strategic partnership.

SC junks anti-HPV vax PIL, says plea has ulterior motive
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:38:28 UTC
06:38:28 KST

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday dismissed a PIL by a doctors' association challenging India's nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme for adolescent girls to protect them against cervical cancer and said it did not behove medical practitioners to take an anti-vaccine stance.
Though the NGO's counsel clarified at the outset that the PIL was not against the vaccination programme but for putting in place mechanisms to take care of adverse reactions and compensation, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant said, "The PIL is definitely anti-vaccine." It gave the option to the lawyer to withdraw or invite adverse comments.
When the counsel continued to argue for prior informed consent of parents of the target population of adolescent girls, the bench said the PIL appeared to have been filed with an ulterior motive and lacked bona fide. It said when there was an established mechanism for taking care of adverse reactions and compensation in individual cases, it did not behove doctors to oppose vaccination when World Health Organisation had recommended it.
The NGO said eminent oncologists have pointed to data that shows cervical cancer incidence has declined over the past three decades.

Across China: Coffee industry brings aroma of success to China's tropical town
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:58 CST
06:36:58 KST

This photo taken on Aug. 20, 2026 shows Robusta coffee cherries in the Xinglong Overseas Chinese Tourism Economic Zone in Wanning City, south China's Hainan Province. (Photo by Wang Yining/Xinhua)
HAIKOU, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- In the heart of Xinglong's coffee culture park, the aroma of roasting beans fills the air as barista Liang Dongru stands over her roaster, eyes focused and movements steady.
"The key is low heat and slow roasting," she said. "In the process, we add butter, white sugar and a little salt, which makes the coffee taste more mellow, rich and smooth."
Xinglong, known as the Xinglong Overseas Chinese Tourism Economic Zone, sits in Hainan, China's southernmost island province. Under the jurisdiction of Wanning City, it has settled generations of returned overseas Chinese and their families since the 1950s.
Those returning compatriots brought back both coffee plants and roasting know-how, fostering coffee cultivation and processing in Xinglong ever since.
Made from locally grown Robusta beans and roasted with butter, sugar and a pinch of salt, Xinglong coffee offers a classic flavor that is both bold and aromatic.
"It's amazing that Xinglong's local annual per-capita coffee consumption has surpassed 200 cups, while the national average is just over 20 cups," said Ye Jian, head of the Xinglong Coffee Industry Association and general manager of CP (Hainan) Xinglong Coffee Industrial Development Co., Ltd.
Coffee, an unconventional beverage for most Chinese before the country's opening-up nearly five decades ago, has grown in popularity since then, with Nestle, one of the biggest coffee companies in the world, introducing instant coffee in the 1980s.
In the late 1990s and early 2000s, international coffee chains like Starbucks and Costa Coffee entered the Chinese market, introducing a new wave of coffee culture.
The country's coffee industry scale reached 354.9 billion yuan (about 52.4 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, up 13.3 percent year on year, with annual per-capita consumption rising to 28.57 cups, according to industry reports.
As a core Robusta-growing region in China, Wanning has in recent years built a comprehensive coffee industry chain, integrating cultivation, processing, e-commerce, local culture and tourism.
As a result, Xinglong coffee has become more than just a beverage -- it is now a cultural symbol of Hainan.
Since 2021, Wanning has been cultivating "Xinglong Barista," with a growing number of young people taking up coffee-making as a career. By July this year, the city has trained 2,476 professionals for the coffee industry.
A large number of practitioners from China's Belt and Road Initiative partner countries have also come to the tropical town to learn about breeding and cultivation techniques for crops such as coffee, pepper and cocoa.
Last December, an international coffee trading and operations center was inaugurated in Xinglong, leveraging the Hainan Free Trade Port's tariff exemption policies.
"Xinglong coffee continues to attract attention from around the world," Ye said. "With more partners, we will advance international cooperation in coffee bean trade and coffee culture exchanges." ■
An aerial drone photo taken on April 22, 2026 shows a view of Xinglong's coffee culture park in Wanning City, south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua)

News Analysis: Africa redraws its place on the map, and on the world stage
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:54 CST
06:36:54 KST

NAIROBI, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- How big is Africa? The answer can differ strikingly from one world map to another.
The question has taken on new weight since Sept. 4, when the United Nations (UN) General Assembly adopted a "Correct the Map" resolution by 164 votes to 1, with 6 abstentions. The measure encourages governments, schools, international organizations and technology companies, among others, to make greater use, where appropriate, of map projections that more accurately reflect the relative sizes of the world's regions.
Analysts say the resolution's significance reaches well beyond cartography. The initiative, proposed by Togo and endorsed by the African Union (AU) before winning overwhelming support at the UN, is in their view both a rare display of the continent speaking with one voice and a measure of Africa's growing ability to place its own concerns on the international agenda.
BEYOND THE MAP
On the Mercator projection, Africa -- a continent roughly 14 times the size of Greenland -- can appear barely larger than the island. Devised in 1569 by cartographer Gerardus Mercator primarily for navigation, the projection preserves angles and directions, making it useful for sailing along a constant bearing. But it inflates regions at high latitudes and visually shrinks Africa and other lands near the equator.
"Maps are never just decorations. They influence education, shape how people perceive the world and the global balance of power," Togo's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation, African Integration and Togolese Abroad Robert Dussey told local media. "Correcting the map means correcting the way we see the world."
Benjamin Mgana, chief editor of foreign news at The Guardian newspaper in Tanzania, told Xinhua that if generations grow up seeing Africa drawn far smaller than it really is, that long-standing visual impression can quietly shape perceptions of the continent's weight and its place in the world.
The UN resolution cited the Equal Earth projection, which depicts the continents' relative sizes more faithfully while keeping the map readable. The AU had earlier endorsed its use.
A more accurate representation of Africa's size would better convey the continent's real significance in demography, economics and geopolitics, Lemmy Nyongesa Mulaku, a scholar of international affairs at the University of Nairobi, said in a recent interview.
"Africa must be represented as it truly is: in its true dimensions and in its rightful place in the world," Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, chairperson of the AU Commission, said in a statement issued on the day of the vote.
The resolution, however, does not brand the Mercator projection as scientifically "wrong." Dussey stressed that it still has practical uses, including in maritime navigation, and that "no one wants to ban it."
The initiative, he said, is about whether a projection that skews perceptions of relative size should remain the default in settings such as education, public information and comparisons between continents.
Dussey said Togo would call on governments, schools, international organizations and companies using mapping technology to switch to maps based on the Equal Earth projection. Over the next six months, Togo plans to consult AU member states and supporters in other regions to promote wider adoption.
Education is a key arena for the change, Leon-Marie Nkolo Ndjodo, an associate professor at the University of Yaounde I in Cameroon, told Xinhua. African countries, he said, need to review teaching content in history, geography, philosophy and economics, as well as in strategic, geopolitical and security studies, so that young people grow up with an accurate picture of the continent's geography.
AFRICA IN ONE VOICE
For the analysts interviewed, the resolution's adoption means more than international support for a single initiative. It also reflects African countries' growing effort to voice common concerns collectively and play a more active part in shaping the global agenda.
"For many years, African countries were often seen mainly as responding to agendas set elsewhere. What we are seeing more and more now is Africa trying to put its own concerns on the international agenda and speak with a stronger collective voice," Mgana said.
"Africa spoke with one voice. That is rare. It is precious. This is pan-Africanism that delivers results," Dussey said. When a continent of 1.4 billion people comes together to correct the image the world holds of it, "the world listens," he added.
In a statement issued on last week, Togo's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation, African Integration and Togolese Abroad said the UN vote demonstrated that "when Africa speaks with one voice and advances an advocacy based on rigor and equity, it is able to rally the international community."
"African countries want greater representation in international institutions, a stronger voice in global decision-making and more space to tell their own stories instead of always being described by others," Mgana said.
This, he believes, points to a broader reassessment across parts of the Global South of systems, institutions and narratives inherited from the past, and a demand for an international order that better matches today's realities.
Starting with a map, Africa is out to change both how the world sees it and how it speaks for itself on the world stage. As Gideon Keter, a former member of Kenya's Parliament, put it: "Our size must finally match our voice, our potential must match our ambition, and our ambition must be matched by action." ■

DR Congo Ebola cases show downward trend, but peak not yet confirmed: health official
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:54 CST
06:36:54 KST

KINSHASA, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is showing an encouraging downward trend in reported cases, but it is still too early to conclude that the epidemic has reached its peak, a senior public health official said Thursday.
Christian Ngandu, a senior official at the National Institute of Public Health (INSP), said absolute case numbers have declined compared with earlier stages of the outbreak.
"We do not think the outbreak will continue along the same trajectory, because when we look at the epidemiological data, the trend is downward in absolute numbers compared with earlier periods," Ngandu told a press conference in Kinshasa. "I did not say that we have reached the peak. I said there is a downward trend."
Ngandu said the trend must be assessed over time and against the evolution of confirmed cases as well as the dates when patients first develop symptoms.
"We need to maintain this trend for it to produce results," he said, warning that any relaxation of response efforts could lead to another surge in infections.
According to the latest official figures, the DRC had recorded 6,843 confirmed Ebola cases as of Sept. 8, including 3,310 deaths and 1,611 recoveries, with the case fatality rate standing at 48.4 percent.
The government is implementing an updated 180-day response plan aimed at sustaining the current trend and bringing the outbreak under control, with greater emphasis on community-level surveillance, contact tracing, prevention and preparedness in areas at risk.
"We believe that, with the messages we have shared and the support of all stakeholders, the population will further take ownership of the fight against this disease, which can be brought under control and will be brought under control within the 180 days set out in the plan," Ngandu said.
The current outbreak, declared in May, has since become the country's largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic on record and the second-largest globally, behind the 2014-2016 epidemic in West Africa. ■

Malaysia's property market stays resilient in H1
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:44 CST
06:36:44 KST

KUALA LUMPUR, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Malaysia's property market remained resilient in the first half of 2026, with 187,320 transactions worth 105.12 billion ringgit (about 25.88 billion U.S. dollars), the National Property Information Center (NAPIC) said on Thursday.
Transaction volume and value were slightly lower than the 196,232 transactions worth 107.68 billion ringgit recorded a year earlier.
The period saw stable prices, continued positive construction activity and growth recorded in several subsectors, supported by the country's strong economic fundamentals and government measures to expand access to home ownership, said NAPIC.
The residential subsector continued to dominate the property market in terms of transaction volume, accounting for the largest share at 59.3 percent.
In line with Malaysia's strong economic growth of 6 percent in the second quarter of 2026, the property market is expected to maintain stable performance, said NAPIC.
This positive outlook is supported by stable price trends, active construction activity and transactions in selected subsectors.
However, it noted that the overall market outlook remains exposed to the impact of changes in the external economic environment and constraints on housing affordability.
Despite challenges arising from global geopolitical uncertainties, Malaysia's strong economic fundamentals and the government's continued strategic initiatives are expected to support the property market in maintaining stable momentum, it said. ■

Nearly 69,000 respiratory infection cases reported in areas hit by Indonesian volcano's ash
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:42 CST
06:36:42 KST

JAKARTA, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Indonesia has recorded 68,919 cumulative cases of acute respiratory infections in areas affected by ash from the erupting Anak Krakatau volcano, health authorities said Thursday.
Health Ministry spokeswoman Widyawati said 17,780 cases were recorded on Sept. 8 alone across 23 districts and cities in four provinces affected by ashfall. Children aged five and under accounted for 14,439 cases, while 54,480 cases were recorded among those older than five, she said.
The Health Ministry said it was conducting health monitoring and public health campaigns in affected areas to reduce risks from prolonged exposure to volcanic ash.
Anak Krakatau erupted again at 9:10 a.m. local time Thursday, according to the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources. Authorities have urged visitors to stay at least 3 km from the active crater.
Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, has remained active since Sept. 4. ■

China moves to curb disorderly low-price competition in key industrial products
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:36 CST
06:36:36 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has issued a notice clarifying cost accounting rules to address disorderly low-price competition in key industrial products. This move is part of broader efforts to curb irrational price wars and ensure fair competition.
The notice, jointly issued by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the State Administration for Market Regulation, clarifies the form and requirements of cost accounting, providing clear guidance for industry and regulators.
The notice says cost accounting should in principle be based on a business operator's individual cost for producing a specific product. If individual cost can not be calculated, the industry average cost should be referenced, allowing for a certain downward margin.
The move comes as the country's efforts to curb "involution-style" competition are showing results, but irrational competition remains prominent in some industrial product manufacturing fields, noted an NDRC official.
"These behaviors are disrupting normal production and business order, potentially allowing 'bad money to drive out good', and harming healthy economic development," the official said.
While current law and rules prohibit low-price dumping and require accounting for individual and industry average costs, they lack detailed provisions on how such accounting should be done. The notice aims to fill that gap and strengthen the institutional foundation for governing disorderly low-price competition.
It is intended to encourage companies to compete on quality and innovation instead of price, promote the rational formation of market prices, and foster a market environment in which high-quality products command premium prices, the NDRC official said.
The notice comes amid signs of improving industrial prices. Latest data showed that the country's producer price index, which measures costs for goods at the factory gate, rose 0.4 percent in August, reversing a 0.7-percent decline in July. The rebound was partly attributed to elevated demand driven by industrial upgrading, the National Bureau of Statistics said. ■

Kenya launches El Nino preparedness plan to safeguard livestock
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:29 CST
06:36:29 KST

NAIROBI, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Kenya on Thursday launched the 2.1-billion-shilling (about 16.2 million U.S. dollars) National Livestock Sector El Nino Preparedness and Anticipatory Action Plan.
Cabinet Secretary for Agriculture and Livestock Development Mutahi Kagwe underscored the government's commitment to protecting Kenya's livestock economy proactively before losses occur.
"The 2023 El Nino and the 2024 long rains floods caused devastating losses to our livestock farmers, destroyed critical infrastructure and triggered disease outbreaks that set back the sector significantly," Kagwe said in a statement issued in Isiolo County in eastern Kenya.
"We therefore need to learn from our experiences, and this is the reason we are determined to ensure that our farmers and pastoralists are not caught unprepared," he added.
The initiative follows advisories from the Kenya Meteorological Department forecasting heightened risks of heavy rainfall, flash floods, and localized inundation across key regions.
Prioritizing proactive intervention over post-disaster recovery, the plan targets 24 high-risk counties with heavy livestock concentrations.
Government projections indicate the strategy will protect livestock value chains, prevent disease outbreaks, minimize herd losses, and cut national disaster recovery costs. ■

Yemen's Houthis deploy forces to strategic Hanish Islands in Red Sea: official
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:25 CST
06:36:25 KST

ADEN, Yemen, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Yemen's Houthi group has deployed forces to the strategic Hanish Islands in the Red Sea following the withdrawal of government naval troops, a Yemeni government official told Xinhua Thursday.
"The naval forces withdrew (on Thursday afternoon), and the Houthis moved in," the official said on condition of anonymity, adding that Houthi forces had begun establishing positions on the islands.
The deployment significantly expands the Houthis' military presence in the southern Red Sea, bringing their forces closer to the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital maritime chokepoint linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
Located north of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and near major international shipping lanes, the Hanish archipelago holds strategic value for monitoring and securing maritime traffic.
Earlier in the day, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea port city of Mocha after fierce fighting forced government troops to retreat south toward Dhubab, between Mocha and Bab al-Mandab. Mocha lies about 70 km north of the strait's narrowest point.
The latest advances mark a major battlefield shift along Yemen's western coast amid one of the sharpest escalations since a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major hostilities.
Yemen's conflict began in late 2014 when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognized government. ■

China Focus: China issues plan to boost strength in finance during 2026-2030 period
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:22 CST
06:36:22 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has issued a plan to strengthen its financial sector during 2026-2030, focusing on preventing financial risks, strengthening financial supervision, and promoting high-quality development.
The office of the Central Financial Commission formulated the plan in coordination with relevant financial authorities, said Lu Lei, deputy governor of the People's Bank of China (PBOC), at a press conference on Thursday.
By 2030, China aims to put in place the overall framework of a modern financial system with Chinese characteristics, ensure that financial regulation policies are well coordinated and effective, optimize the structure of the financial system, ensure rigorous and effective financial supervision, and make financial risk prevention and control targeted and efficient, according to the plan.
Other goals for 2030 include continued improvements in the quality and effectiveness of financial support for economic and social development, a comprehensive legal framework for the financial sector, steady expansion of high-standard financial opening up, and continued increases in the sector's international influence and competitiveness.
The plan aims to largely establish a highly adaptive, competitive, and inclusive modern financial system with Chinese characteristics by 2035, laying a solid foundation for further boosting China's strength in finance.
Key tasks outlined in the plan include improving the financial macro-regulation system, strengthening financial supervision, effectively preventing and defusing financial risks, serving the real economy more proactively and effectively, promoting high-quality development of the financial sector, and expanding high-standard financial opening up.
MONETARY POLICY FRAMEWORK
Regarding monetary policy, Lu said China will continue to transform and improve its monetary policy framework to better adapt it to the profound changes in the country's economic and financial structures.
The PBOC, China's central bank, will remain firmly committed to maintaining currency value stability and thereby promoting economic growth and providing effective support for the high-quality development of the real economy. It will enhance its base money supply mechanism and reserve requirement system, and conduct open market operations with greater flexibility and precision, Lu said.
China will maintain its managed floating exchange rate system, allow the market to play a decisive role in exchange rate formation, and guard against herd behavior and the self-reinforcement of irrational expectations, he said.
The central bank will also improve monetary policy communication and expectations management, further develop credible, regular and institutionalized policy communication mechanisms, and make monetary policy communication easier to understand and more authoritative.
A STRONGER, MORE INCLUSIVE CAPITAL MARKET
China will accelerate a new round of capital market reform and opening up and strive to establish a new pattern of high-quality development and achieve marked improvements in the market's overall strength and international competitiveness by 2030, the 40th anniversary of the establishment of China's capital market, said Li Chao, vice chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, at the press conference.
The securities regulator will introduce more inclusive rules for stock issuance and listings and for mergers and acquisitions, and work to make the A-share market the preferred listing venue for high-quality domestic companies, Li said.
Since the beginning of the year, medium- and long-term funds, including social security funds, annuity funds and insurance funds, have purchased more than 600 billion yuan (about 88.4 billion U.S. dollars) worth of A-shares on a net basis. The market value of their holdings of tradable A-shares has increased 12.5 percent since the end of 2025, Li said.
FINANCIAL STABILITY AND OPENING UP
In the banking and insurance sectors, China will prudently prevent and control risks in key areas, take forceful, orderly and effective steps to prevent and defuse risks at local small and medium-sized financial institutions, and firmly guard against major risk events, said Cong Lin, deputy head of the National Financial Regulatory Administration.
Financial institutions will be guided to shift from a model of scale-driven, high-speed expansion to one focused on quality and performance, while strong action will be taken against price wars, illegal commission rebates and practices involving excessively high interest rates and returns, Cong said.
Cong said differentiated measures will be taken to optimize the system of financial institutions, clarify the permitted scope of business and prohibited conduct for different types of institutions, and guide them to focus on their core businesses and pursue differentiated development. These steps aim to enhance the adaptability and competitiveness of the financial system.
China has achieved basic convertibility for direct investment transactions, said Li Bin, deputy head and spokesperson of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
Cross-border securities investment arrangements now include institutional investor programs, market connectivity mechanisms and direct access to domestic markets for overseas investors, while all forms of cross-border financing are subject to macro-prudential management, Li said.
More broadly, during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), China's banking and insurance sectors provided more than 170 trillion yuan in additional financing support to the real economy through loans, bonds and equity, while the broader financial sector advanced reform and opening up, strengthened supervision and made progress in addressing risks in key areas, officials said at Thursday's press conference.
China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for accelerating the development of a modern financial system with Chinese characteristics. The plan emphasizes aligning the growth of social financing and the money supply with targets for economic growth and overall price levels, as well as increasing the flexibility of the renminbi exchange rate while maintaining its basic stability at an adaptive and balanced level.
It also calls for expanding patient capital, improving the supporting system for the entry of medium- and long-term funds into the capital market, and strengthening financial supervision and the prevention and resolution of financial risks. ■

Yang Shuyu (C) of China goes for a basket against Marieme Badiane (L) of France during the quarterfinal match at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 in Berlin, Germany, Sept. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/He Canling)
BERLIN, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- France ended China's FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup campaign with a commanding 90-61 quarterfinal victory on Thursday, setting up a semifinal against either host Germany or Belgium.
China stayed within striking distance during a competitive opening quarter, with Han Xu and Yang Shuyu carrying much of the scoring load, but France seized control in the second period and steadily pulled away.
An 11-0 run gave France the first double-digit lead of the game and swung the momentum firmly in its favor. China struggled to keep its opponent off the offensive glass and repeatedly surrendered possession through turnovers, allowing France to establish a 48-31 halftime lead.
China needed a strong response after the break but was unable to produce a sustained run to cut the deficit. Zhang Ziyu contributed seven points and eight rebounds, but also committed seven turnovers in 18 minutes.
Han led China with 21 points and nine rebounds on 8-of-13 shooting, while Yang added 19 points and five assists. The pair accounted for 40 of China's 61 points, with no other Chinese player reaching double figures.
France benefited from a more balanced offensive display. Marine Johannes and Janelle Salaun scored 15 points apiece, with Johannes also handing out seven assists. Gabby Williams collected 14 points and seven rebounds, while Leila Lacan added 12 points.
China's difficulties in protecting the ball and finishing defensive possessions proved costly. France grabbed 19 offensive rebounds, while China committed 20 turnovers, helping the French attempt 79 field goals compared with China's 50.
France remained firmly in control throughout the second half and comfortably closed out the victory to secure a place in the last four.
The defeat brought China's tournament to an end with three wins and two losses. China had reached the quarterfinals by edging Puerto Rico 75-72 in Wednesday's qualification round.
France will face the winner of Thursday's quarterfinal between Germany and Belgium in Saturday's semifinal. ■

KINSHASA, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- At least 21 students were killed and several others seriously injured in a fire that broke out Thursday in Bukavu, capital of the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)'s South Kivu Province, local media reported.
The DRC Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship confirmed that the fire in the Funu area of Bukavu affected the Furaah and Ujamaa schools, which claimed several lives, including students, and left many injured.
"The death toll remains provisional and may be revised as information gathered from various sources is consolidated and verified. The exact circumstances and cause of the fire are also still under investigation," the ministry said in a statement.
According to local media, 15 students from the two schools were killed in a stampede as they tried to flee the flames. Some of the injured were reported to be in serious condition, while others suffering from smoke inhalation were receiving medical treatment.
The education ministry has instructed relevant services to assess the situation at the affected schools, identify the immediate needs of students, teachers and school communities, and assist those affected and ensure the continuity of learning.
Bukavu is currently under the control of the March 23 Movement rebel group. ■

Thai central bank rolls out joint framework to curb fraud, money laundering
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
05:36:12 CST
06:36:12 KST

BANGKOK, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's central bank said on Thursday that it has joined forces with 11 financial industry associations to escalate measures against illicit use of the financial system under a newly developed framework.
Bank of Thailand governor Vitai Ratanakorn said the initiative aims to keep Thailand's financial system stable, secure, and trusted while shielding the public from harm linked to misuse of financial services.
Under the framework, Vitai said participating parties must set clear governance policies to prevent system misuse and step up scrutiny of high-risk cash transactions. Firms will also deploy technology to proactively flag unusual transactions and build a shared database of high-risk individuals linked to the Central Fraud Registry.
In a statement, the central bank said it will tighten system-wide supervisory standards, expand use of data and technology to detect high-risk transactions, and promote information sharing among institutions to close regulatory loopholes exploited by fraud networks.
Signatories include the Thai Bankers' Association, the Association of International Banks, the Government Financial Institutions Association, the Thai E-Payment Trade Association, the Thai Association of Foreign Exchange and Financial Services, and six associations representing non-bank lenders.
The groups will jointly issue industry-wide anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing guidelines and work with community networks to build financial resilience among vulnerable populations.
The central bank also noted that the coordinated push, paired with public financial-literacy campaigns, is intended to reinforce long-term safety, resilience, and confidence in the Southeast Asian nation's financial system while balancing impacts on legitimate customers, market competition, and innovation. ■

Data farmers taking advantage of Russia's fuel crisis — GFCN
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:36:08 UTC
06:36:08 KST

MOSCOW, September 11. /TASS/. Amid Russia's fuel crisis, fake gas station maps have appeared online to farm data from Russian citizens, Vladimir Tabak, president of the Global Fact-Checking Network (GFCN), told TASS ahead of the Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum.
"There are currently some fuel supply difficulties in our regions. Numerous phishing websites are offering counterfeit fuel vouchers, and unverified sites with completely bogus gas station maps are operating solely to collect users’ data," he said.
Tabak described this as "a striking example of how a situation arising offline can prompt the creation of projects that subsequently pose a fairly serious threat to citizens and the state, as systematic efforts begin to target the country as a whole."
"I think no sphere is immune to this problem today. But the most vulnerable areas are those involving security, political processes and social issues," he stressed.
The Global Fact-Checking Network brings together experts and fact-checking organizations worldwide. The association was founded by the TASS news agency, the nonprofit organization Dialogue Regions and the New Media Workshop to combat disinformation. More than 125 journalists from 55 countries already collaborate with GFCN on fact-checking.
The international Dialogue about Fakes 4.0 forum will take place on September 22 at the Russia National Center in Moscow. TASS is the event’s strategic partner.

Germany Moves to Block Far-Right AfD From Accessing Classified War Plans
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:34:12 UTC
06:34:12 KST

- Category
- World
Germany Moves to Block Far-Right AfD From Accessing Classified War Plans
Germany’s Defense Ministry is exploring measures to block the state premier’s office in Saxony-Anhalt from accessing highly sensitive wartime crisis-response plans, Bloomberg reported on September 10.
The restriction would take effect if the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) takes power in the region.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The blueprint, known as OPLAN, is a classified 1,000-page document that outlines joint defense strategies by German and NATO authorities in the event of a military crisis or war. It requires a coordinated response between federal and regional officials, as Germany serves as a central hub for transferring NATO troops eastward during an alliance defense operation.
German domestic intelligence agencies have long scrutinized the Alternative for Germany (AfD) over its extensive ties to Moscow and its potential role as a conduit for Russian influence. The AfD has faced mounting accusations of operating as a “Trojan horse” for the Kremlin, with senior officials warning that the party frequently abuses parliamentary inquiries to gather sensitive intelligence on Germany’s critical infrastructure—information that directly benefits Russian hybrid warfare operations.
The party consistently opposes EU integration, rejects military aid to Ukraine, and advocates for restoring deep economic ties with Russia, while multiple AfD figures have been investigated for accepting funds from Kremlin-linked media networks.
The full version of the OPLAN is available to the leaders of Germany’s 16 states, with local authorities holding access to relevant regional sections.
Defense Minister Boris Pistorius told defense policy experts during a closed-door meeting this week that he aims to prevent an AfD-led state government from obtaining the ability to pass the planning document to Russia. Decision-makers anticipate that OPLAN could be activated in the event of an escalation with Moscow, according to Bloomberg.
The move follows the AfD’s strong performance in Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt, where the anti-immigration party secured 44% of the vote—falling just three seats short of an outright majority. Bloomberg reported that the parliamentary maneuvering next month could hand the far right executive power in a German region for the first time since World War II.
Germany’s security establishment and domestic intelligence agencies already consider parts of the AfD a threat to the constitutional order.
The party’s embrace of Moscow, which includes rejecting military aid for Ukraine and advocating for the restoration of Russian economic ties, has drawn sharp scrutiny. German officials have spent months deliberating how to safeguard sensitive security data if the party assumes control of state-level operations, with options reportedly including deleting or reclassifying certain intelligence, Bloomberg wrote.
The Defense Ministry declined to comment further on the classified plan.
Concerns over Russian political influence in Germany are not limited to the far right, as ties between Moscow and former German leadership remain a point of friction. Аormer Chancellor Gerhard Schröder previously made an unannounced visit to Moscow, coinciding with the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum.
The trip followed a proposal by Vladimir Putin suggesting Schröder serve as an EU peace mediator—a role immediately rejected by both the EU and Ukraine.

Post-GFC era of low rates is over and hike in November expected, ANZ says
Central banks, bond markets, and the conflict in the Middle East dominated the week, and together they pointed to an increasingly challenging macro dynamic of higher inflation, sustained higher yields, and slower growth, ANZ Research said.
Domestically, markets largely priced in a rate hike from the RBA later this month, ANZ researchers said, adding the team is "less convinced" and "is retaining our November call", where it predicts a 0.25 percentage point interest rate hike.
"First, the Board has a strong preference for moving in Statement on Monetary Policy meetings," ANZ noted.
"Second, the RBA's most recent public comments on the seasonal adjustment of the monthly CPI point to a little uncertainty, which suggests the quarterly print (due at the end of October) will likely carry more weight.
"And third, with policy clearly restrictive and there being only five weeks between the September and November meetings, there is less urgency to tighten now than there was in March. We would also view a September hike as a very hawkish signal."
ANZ added that the re-escalation of the conflict in the Middle East does complicate matters.
"The RBA's frame of reference has been to view the conflict as an upside inflation risk much more than a downside growth risk," it said.
"With Brent crude above $US105/barrel, the RBA is likely to be even more concerned about second-round inflation risks.
"Bond yields pushed higher this week, with the US 10y at 4.96% and the Australian 10y above 5.35%.
"We see much of the re-pricing in long-end yields as reflecting expectations of higher-for-longer policy rates but also markets seeking more compensation to reflect the global combination of large government borrowing requirements, hyperscaler debt supply, and greater policy uncertainty."
ANZ now expects that after a hike to 4.60% in November, the RBA will likely only ease twice (once in late 2027 and once in early 2028), taking the cash rate to a "low" 4.10%.
"That would see the average cash rate over 2026–28 much higher than most of the post-GFC 'low rates' era," it said.
RBA more likely to keep rates on hold this month: analyst
Betashares's chief economist, David Bassanese, says the case for a September rate hike remains unconvincing and the RBA is, at this stage, still more likely to keep rates on hold.
The higher-than-expected July CPI report could simply be monthly volatility, especially given the more benign Q2 inflation outcome, Mr Bassanese said.
"And while Q2 GDP was a touch higher than expected, it still revealed an economy growing at a below-trend pace," he noted.
"House prices are still falling and, unlike past interest-rate driven cycles, no-one can be confident the decline will remain modest given the massive property tax changes in the federal budget.
"This week’s business and consumer surveys also revealed a notable buckling in confidence."
Mr Bassanese added that, in the short term, rising oil prices would cause volatility in both equities and bonds, with the cure obviously being a cessation of hostilities in the Middle East.
However, that seemed to be a constant mirage for markets, he said.

Multiple job holders? One reason is fewer hours per job
We already knew the concerning data that more Australians than ever hold multiple jobs.
It's the highest in both number (1 million people) and percentage: 6.9%
Among younger people aged 20–24, it's even higher: 11.2%.
So an interesting addition to the data comes from anonymised and aggregated workforce data across healthcare, hospitality, retail and services from scheduling tool Deputy.
Its data suggests that changes in shift-work patterns provide context to the numbers:
- Across all sectors, total hours worked fell 7.7% month on month — the steepest decrease of 2026 — but employers locked in shifts an average of 8.3 days ahead (up 24.1% from July) to give workers more certainty.
- Healthcare drove the strongest changes, scheduling 13.5 days ahead to help scarce care workers balance second jobs. Specifically, in-home care lifted its average notice period by 102% (to 12.1 days) and NDIS providers by 51% (to 10.2 days).
- Retail and Services both added workers while reducing hours per employee, a sign that work is being spread across more people rather than concentrated in fewer roles.
- Hospitality was part of a universal cooldown in shift volume, contributing to the first month in 2026 where all four major sectors declined in hours worked. However, like other sectors, hospitality venues rostered further ahead than they did in July to offer workers more stability.
There is obviously a little guff in information from a scheduling software business about the importance of scheduling, but Ciaran Hale, chief technology officer at Deputy, makes a good point about the reality facing people working multiple jobs:
"The 8.3-day rostering figure is the most important number in this month's (data)," he said in a statement.
"It shows employers are starting to treat certainty as part of the employment offer. For many hourly workers, a second or third role is no longer unusual. When one roster does not fill a week, people need enough notice to coordinate another job, caring responsibilities or study. Predictability is what makes those working arrangements viable. Employers appear to understand that. They are absorbing higher award rates by planning more deliberately, not simply by cutting people loose.
In what is reality, but I can't help but be a bit deflated by: employers that lean into helping their staff work multiple jobs are more likely to retain them.
"The businesses that give their teams a roster they can build a life around will be the ones best placed to retain them."
In other interesting notes, "terminations fell 21.4%, the lowest monthly total of 2026, while new hires were effectively flat".
The report said retail and services "both added workers while reducing hours per employee, a sign that work is being spread across more people rather than concentrated in fewer roles".
Copper 3‑month rolling futures tumble from record highs: analyst
Copper 3‑month rolling futures reached a record high of $US14,853 per tonne in intraday trading on Thursday, the highest price year‑to‑date, according to Vivek Dhar, head of Commodities and Sustainability Research at Commonwealth Bank.
However, prices tumbled by around 4.5% overnight to $US14,183/t, the CommBank noted.
"We expect that the upward trajectory in copper prices was clipped by a combination of macroeconomic factors, namely the spike in Brent crude to about $109/bbl, but also due to speculation around copper prices' steady uplift being a 'speculative bubble' rather than related to supply‑demand fundamentals," said Mr Dhar.
He said the key drivers supporting prices had been predominantly supply‑related.
"The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) estimates that in the first half of 2026 global mined copper production decreased by 1.1% y/y, with concentrate production in Chile, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Indonesia falling by 8% y/y, 34% y/y and 32% y/y respectively."
Another key driver supporting prices currently was the movement in global stocks of refined copper, Mr Dhar said.
"Over the last 24 months total exchange stocks, which include those in the COMEX, LME and SHFE exchanges have lifted from about 575kt to 1.06Mt in the two years to 10 September 2026," he said.
"The rise in volume is almost entirely due to the rise in COMEX stocks in the US, where inventory levels at the end of August 2026, have now exceeded the last peak in August 2003."
He said this occurred due to "the expectation that the Trump administration will place a 15% import tariff on all refined copper products from the start of 2027" after previously placing Section 232 tariffs on semi‑finished and derivative copper products last August.

"According to Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), China's imports of copper scrap, as well as its domestic scrap production have increased month on month since June.
"This, along with increased concentrate and refined supply over the remainder of the year and into 2027 is likely to alleviate tight supply conditions, which in turn will support lower copper prices."
BOJ set to lift rates next week but offer few clues on terminal
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to raise interest rates next week, most likely by 25 basis points, and may signal faster future tightening if price pressures heighten risks of an inflation overshoot, according to four sources familiar with its thinking.
A hike to 1.25% would bring the BOJ's policy rate to levels unseen in 31 years. A rate hike just three months after its last one in June also suggests a faster pace of tightening, especially if the bank raises rates again this year.
Many in the central bank saw conditions falling into place for another rate hike with the economy on course for a moderate recovery and price pressure building, sources said.
The BOJ also expected financial conditions to remain loose even if it raises interest rates to 1.25%, the sources added.
While the yen's recent rebound could ease pressure on prices by moderating import-cost increases, the currency's past declines and a renewed surge in fuel prices would keep the BOJ on guard over inflation risks, they said.
"With underlying inflation so close to 2%, the BOJ needs to be extra mindful of upside price risks," said one of the sources, a view echoed by three more sources.
The BOJ raised interest rates to 1% in June and pledged to push borrowing costs higher if economic and price developments align with its baseline projections.
While it kept rates steady in July, the BOJ signalled a strong chance of a near-term hike by warning of the risk of an inflation overshoot due to price pressures from the Middle East conflict, a weak yen and brisk AI-related demand.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to hike rates to 1.25% at the September 17-18 meeting, 1.5% by end-March next year and then to 1.75% in the second quarter of 2027.
Most saw the terminal rate at least at 1.75%.
With markets having fully priced in a September hike, some market players had bet the BOJ could spring a surprise by going with a bigger-than-expected 50-basis-point hike.
With no immediate risk of an abrupt jump in wage and price growth, however, the BOJ would likely opt for the usual 25-point hike next week and wait for more data to gauge whether another near-term increase would be necessary, the sources said.
"Underlying inflation is about to reach 2%, but we don't see it sharply overshooting that level," BOJ board member Kazuyuki Masu said on Thursday, suggesting that he saw no imminent signs of a spike in inflation that warranted a big hike next week.

LG defends smart-TV features amid audio surveillance allegations
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:33:28 UTC
06:33:28 KST

LG defends smart-TV features amid audio surveillance allegations
Recent allegations into LG’s smart TVs have raised new questions about the nonconsensual data it harvests.
South Korean consumer-electronics company LG has denied allegations that its smart televisions record ambient conversations, listen while on standby and store recordings for later transmission.
On Wednesday, the company told Al Jazeera that voice data is only recorded when a user presses and holds the voice button on the TV remote or activates its “Hi LG” wake word, after the user has activated the Far-Field voice recognition feature.
“Other than these instances, the TVs do not collect or record ambient conversations,” LG said, adding that voice data is only processed via explicit user commands.
“The audio is immediately deleted if the wake word is not recognised,” the company said.
The statement comes after a 135-minute investigative report released on Monday by a popular tech media outlet and YouTube channel, Gamers Nexus, with Level1Techs and independent security researchers. The investigation examined LG televisions’ data collection and security systems, raising questions about how the devices handle users’ private information.
By analysing network traffic and software, the researchers purport to have discovered that these televisions actively track users and harvest a glut of local network data, including audio transcripts.
Inside LG’s controversial tracking system
Gamers Nexus said its researchers were able to record audio through an LG television while it was in a state of hibernation, meaning that even if the microphone switch on the TV is turned off, other microphones exposed to the TV might not be, such as the remote.
The result, Gamers Nexus says, is “216,000,000 Spy TVs” in the US alone.
On its website, LG says it has 49 million smarts TVs in the US and 216 million globally.
Recorded background noise in the room, including as far as 12 metres (40 feet) away from the TV, was also being archived, they said.
Yash Vekaria, a computer science researcher at the University of California, Davis, says that because TVs stay in homes for years, often past their update support, “prompt patching from LG matters”.
“This vulnerability can allow sniffing [of] much more critical conversations … Imagine government officials discussing national security in their hotel room [next to an] LG TV”, Vekaria said.
The researchers further alleged that unmatched wake-word interactions or unclear sounds could remain stored locally, transcribed and preserved on the device as plain text in case the local network is disconnected and uploaded later to LG servers.
Copies can stay in temporary storage spaces, known as buffers, without the user knowing, Vekaria said.
Privacy risks generally stem from poor design and selective disclosure. The more disconcerting threat lies in a compromised device, Vekaria added, which could be made to execute any command its hardware allows.
The researchers also said they found text transcripts derived from audio captured by the television, even after 10-15 seconds of silence after invoking “Hi LG”.
The claims have not been independently verified by Al Jazeera.
“It raises a question of purpose,” says Vekaria, “a voice command is only useful in real time, so audio queued for later upload is presumably being kept for something else, such as logging, analytics or model training. LG should explain what”.
Vekaria says he is not aware of any concrete evidence that ambient audio or transcripts feed into LG’s advertising or profiling systems.
“What we do know is that LG runs an advertising business built on household data, including the Automatic Content Recognition [ACR] tracking documented in our research, and that its voice pipeline appears to capture and retain more than users would expect.”
Still, there may be simpler explanations, he says, “such as diagnostics or improving speech recognition … but even those involve keeping recordings from people’s homes without meaningful consent”.
The smart home is listening
The researchers also said that the televisions scanned home networks for other devices and collected information including internal IP addresses, nearby Wi-Fi networks and location data.
LG said scanning for nearby devices is a “standard” smart-TV function.
Device discovery can serve “legitimate functions” such as screen casting, media sharing and connecting smart-home products, like Amazon’s Alexa, said Anna Maria Mandalari, a lecturer in communications and networking at University College London.
LG stated that ACR, voice recognition and interest-based advertising are all “separate features”, each requiring “explicit user opt-in consent” and each of which can be disabled through the TV’s settings.
Depending on how device discovery is implemented, Mandalari said, a television may “obtain the names, addresses, manufacturers and types of other devices on a household network” – information that can reveal the composition of a home and help “create a broader profile of its occupants”.
LG’s advertising arm, LG Ad Solutions, has openly marketed the breadth of information it can derive from connected households. Corporate videos featured in the Gamers Nexus investigation show LG representatives saying: “We know who is in the LG household,” and, “We know which devices are there.”
LG told Al Jazeera that it was “committed to providing transparency” and that it rejected “deceptive practices”.

Peru joins US-led ‘Shield of the Americas’ security alliance
The Fujimori administration is the latest right-wing government to join the alliance, which promises a more aggressive approach against crime in the Americas.
Peru will join the “Shield of the Americas”, a regional security alliance led by the United States that shares intelligence and cooperates in military operations against drug cartels.
Keiko Fujimori, Peru’s recently elected right-wing leader, announced the move on Thursday after talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3US forces sink vessel ‘linked to Ecuador criminal gang’
- list 2 of 3Marco Rubio says US seeks more economic and security ties in Latin America
- list 3 of 3US announces $45m in security funding, additional naval vessels for Ecuador
“We appreciate this opportunity [to join the initiative], because for us, having previously had to tackle terrorism, [we] know how difficult it is to confront criminality today,” Fujimori said.
Her government also awarded Rubio the Order of the Sun, one of the country’s highest civilian honours.
Rubio’s visit to the Peruvian capital, Lima, caps his three-day, three-country tour of South America to shore up ties between US President Donald Trump and conservative allies in the region.
The diplomat praised Fujimori’s decision to join the Shield of the Americas, also known as the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (ACCC), which has advocated for greater military involvement in the fight against crime.
“It is a shield against these threats to the sovereignty of these independent nations,” Rubio explained.
“It is a shield against these transnational criminal groups that, in many cases, have more money and better military equipment than the state. That is unacceptable, and the only way to defeat it is to confront it forcefully.”
Fujimori, a former first lady and the daughter of former President Alberto Fujimori, was sworn into office in July after campaigning heavily on security-related issues.
Peru is the world’s second-largest producer of cocaine, behind Colombia, and reports of crimes like extortion have spiked in recent years.
But Washington’s involvement in the region remains a controversial prospect, given its history of past interventions and its support of right-wing leaders accused of human rights abuses.
Al Jazeera correspondent Teresa Bo explained that the closer cooperation has also raised concerns about the prospect of eroding Latin American sovereignty.
“This has generated lots of fear among many people in this part of the world of what a greater influence of the United States, of what a military influence of the United States, could bring about,” she said.
Rubio attempted to tamp down those concerns during his visit, saying the US would only intervene with the permission of local authorities.
“We’re not going to do anything that our partners don’t ask us to do,” Rubio said. “We don’t want to do less than what you ask of us, but we’re not going to do more than what you ask of us.”
Nevertheless, in Lima, protesters gathered outside the government house where Fujimori’s meeting with Rubio was taking place. Some carried signs that read, “Marco Rubio out of Peru, no to Shield of the Americas.”
“We have said that Peru is nobody’s colony, and it is not the back garden of any country in the world,” Soledad Lozano, one of the protesters, said.
The Trump administration has also indicated that it would like countries like Peru distance themselves from China, which overtook the US as Peru’s primary trading partner.
In February, for instance, the Trump administration criticised Peru for allowing China to construct a mega-port in Chancay, warning that “cheap Chinese money costs sovereignty”.
“China has major investments in Peru right now,” Bo explained. “It controls a port that is 80km away from Lima, and what the US is trying to do is increase its presence in the Western Hemisphere and to try to cut a bit of economic dependency that many countries in Latin America have with China.”
Peru is critical not only to US security strategy in Latin America, but also to its economic interests. It is an important source of mineral resources, as the world’s third-largest producer of copper.
In January, Washington designated Peru a major non-NATO ally, and the US State Department approved a possible $1.5bn foreign military sale for work at Callao Naval Base, Peru’s main naval hub near Lima.

The Global South cannot afford to let its maritime border disputes fester
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:30:05 UTC
06:30:05 KST

Makane Moïse Mbengue is professor of international law at the Faculty of Law of the University of Geneva and director of the Department of International Law and International Organisation.
The ocean looks like peace from afar and truth up close, they say. But beneath the waves, the map of the world’s oceans is far less settled than it looks. Today, dozens of sea borders remain unresolved. Like so many conflicts, they owe their origins to complicated questions of where one country’s territory ends, and another’s begins.
Many involve overlapping claims to areas rich in resources; and a disproportionate number concern the waters of the Global South. Africa’s coastline is a stark example. The continent has the highest number of unsettled sea boundaries. These disputes are liabilities, and at the worst possible time.
The conflict in the Middle East has shaken energy markets around the world but nowhere has been more exposed than the Global South. This vulnerability is why governments in these regions can no longer afford to leave these borders unsettled. As future chokepoints preventing much-needed resource development, they also risk confrontation and create grey zones ripe for illegal fishing.
Global conflicts are not just disrupting energy markets, but the legal order that maritime security, and much else, depends on. The need for governments to engage with these disputes has rarely been more urgent, and there is no better time for the Global South to show how international law can and should provide solutions.
Lessons can be drawn from recent developments in the Gulf of Thailand. In May, Thailand withdrew from a 25-year-old memorandum of understanding with Cambodia to resolve their maritime boundary and peacefully develop undersea energy resources valued at over US$300 billion. Rather than escalate, Cambodia initiated compulsory conciliation proceedings under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
Thailand accepted the offer in June, and a commission of international legal experts has now formed to hear the dispute and peacefully work towards a resolution. Cambodia, the smaller nation of the two and in open conflict with Thailand months ago, has secured a hearing on a dispute it could never have won by force.

Kazakhstan was not admitted to Eurovision 2027, despite applying for full membership in the EBU

Kazakhstan was not admitted to Eurovision 2027, despite applying for full membership in the EBU
Kyiv • UNN
Kazakhstan will not make its debut at the Eurovision Song Contest 2027 because its broadcaster does not meet the requirements for full EBU membership. Khabar remains an associate member.
Kazakhstan will not be able to make its debut at the adult Eurovision Song Contest in 2027 after its public broadcaster "Khabar" failed to meet the requirements for full membership in the European Broadcasting Union. Politico reports, as UNN writes.
Details
The EBU explained that Kazakhstan is not part of the European Broadcasting Area, is not a member of the Council of Europe, and does not have official observer status in the organization.
Thus, the "Khabar" agency currently does not meet the requirements for full membership
Canada made it, Kazakhstan did not
"Khabar" remains an EBU associate member. Kazakhstan has already participated in the Junior Eurovision Song Contest five times—from 2018 to 2022—coming second twice. However, associate membership does not automatically grant the right to compete in the adult contest.
Kazakhstan has introduced paid entry permits for Russians06.09.26, 07:15 • 10942 views
At the same time, geographic location is not a determining criterion. Australia participates in Eurovision by special invitation, while Canada became a full EBU member after the rules were changed and is due to make its debut in the contest in 2027. Canada meets the requirements, in particular thanks to its observer status in the Council of Europe.
Thus, Kazakhstan remains outside the main Eurovision for now, while its broadcaster retains only the status of an EBU associate member. The union did not specify whether the country might be given the opportunity to join the contest in the future.

Ukraine hits key Russia-Iran logistics hub in Caspian Sea, damages three Russian warships
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
21:29:41 UTC
06:29:41 KST

Ukraine says its forces struck Russia’s Makhachkala port on the Caspian Sea and confirmed damage to three Russian warships in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk in a series of long-range attacks.
Ukraine’s General Staff said the Makhachkala Sea Commercial Port in Russia’s Dagestan was hit overnight on 10 September, with a fire recorded at the site. The extent of the damage is still being assessed.
The Special Operations Forces (SSO) said Ukrainian units struck oil infrastructure at the port in a joint operation with other Defense Forces. The port’s oil terminal handles tankers with a capacity of up to 10,000 tonnes, while an oil depot is located nearby, according to the SSO.
Makhachkala is Russia’s only ice-free deepwater port on the Caspian Sea and operates year-round. The General Staff said it is an important link in the Russia-Iran logistics corridor, which Moscow uses to bypass Western sanctions.
According to the General Staff, the route is used to transport military-related cargo in both directions, including components and Shahed-type attack drones from Iran to Russia, and explosives, drone components, and ammunition from Russia to Iran. A base of Russia’s Caspian Flotilla is also located near the port.
The SSO said damaging the port’s oil infrastructure could reduce Russia’s ability to use the Caspian Sea to transport and transship energy resources.
Fire Point, a Ukrainian drone manufacturer, said Ukrainian forces used its FP-1 drones in the attack. The company said Makhachkala had been used as a transit point for Iranian attack drones delivered to Russia by sea before being moved onward for use against Ukraine.
Fire Point also said the port handled more than 2.9 million tonnes of cargo in the first eight months of 2026, including more than 2.08 million tonnes of oil.
Three Russian warships hit in Novorossiysk
Ukraine’s General Staff also said further analysis of data confirmed damage inflicted on three Russian warships in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk on 9 September, along with fuel-oil storage facilities at the port.
The General Staff identified the vessels as the small sea minesweeper Zheleznyakov, the frigate Admiral Essen, and the Project 11711 landing ship Pyotr Morgunov.
Visual analysis published by Exilenova+ reported strikes on another Russian warship, the Buyan-M-class corvette, as well as confirming strikes on the frigates Admiral Essen and Admiral Makarov. The outlet said the Essen was hit in its superstructure and caught fire.
The Buyan-M class is capable of carrying Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. Russia has used such ships to launch strikes against Ukraine.
The Ukrainian General Staff said operations against key Russian military targets are continuing.

Black Sea blockade could trigger global food crisis - Zelensky
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
20:40:00 UTC
05:40:00 KST

Black Sea blockade could trigger global food crisis - Zelensky
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said this on Telegram, referring to his conversation with American journalist Fareed Zakaria during the 2026 Yalta European Strategy meeting, according to Ukrinform.
"Prolonging the war is now a challenge not only for Ukraine, it is a challenge for Russia's economy and a challenge for everyone in the world. Take the example of the Black Sea blockade. Today, we have a blocked food corridor. It is almost blocked on the Ukrainian side, and it is blocked on the Russian side. And this is a challenge for everyone. I have spoken with Egypt, India, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, the Emirates," Zelensky said.
He stressed that Ukrainians would not be left without food.
"The price of grain will fall because exports will be expensive, the infrastructure for these sales will be complicated, and logistics will be terrible. This will be very difficult for us," Zelensky said.
At the same time, he noted that, apart from Ukraine, other countries would find themselves in a much worse situation, as they would simply have no food: "Many peoples will have nothing to eat, even if they have money. This is true. It will be Hormuz, only agricultural. And this is a serious problem. This issue should not be resolved by Ukraine alone. Because it is a challenge for many."
He stressed that agriculture and energy are two challenges facing the entire world today.
"And if peace is impossible today because one person does not want it, the issues of an energy truce and food security can be resolved. Such decisions can be made. We raised these issues a long time ago, but now they are extremely relevant," Zelensky added.

Zelensky: If Russia strikes energy infrastructure, Ukraine will respond
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
20:25:00 UTC
05:25:00 KST

Zelensky: If Russia strikes energy infrastructure, Ukraine will respond
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said this on Telegram, referring to his conversation with American journalist Fareed Zakaria during the 2026 Yalta European Strategy meeting, according to Ukrinform.
"Ukraine has learned to find ways to respond appropriately to Russian strikes. I am not comparing this with the humanitarian catastrophes they are causing today. Ukraine does not do that. Nevertheless, Ukraine is capable of responding to any operation they carry out against us," Zelensky said.
He noted that Russia knows: "If they strike – and they are preparing to strike our energy system in winter – Russia will receive the same in return. If they cause blackouts for us, we will try to respond appropriately."
According to him, there is an alternative that Ukraine has always supported – negotiations.
"The negotiation process should be about ending the war. And if Russia does not want to end it, our partners need to find a way to engage with it. If that is difficult to achieve, then at least today we need to move step by step. Unblock the Black Sea and find a possibility for an energy truce, in which the energy infrastructure of both countries is protected," Zelensky said.
He stressed that the track on exchanging prisoners of war and returning civilians, journalists and other citizens who were captured and imprisoned in the Russian Federation, as well as returning Ukrainian children, must also continue.
"This humanitarian track is very important. We must move toward a trilateral meeting," Zelensky added.
According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the situation in Russia's oil refining industry is deteriorating as sanctions hamper its recovery from increasingly intensive and precise Ukrainian drone strikes.
